question.text: The line $x=2 y$ intersects the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{4}+y^{2}=1$ at the points $P$ and $Q .$ The equation of the circle with $P Q$ as diameter is

solution.text: Solving $x=2 y$ and $\frac{x^{2}}{4}+y^{2}=1$ Put $x=2 y$ in Eq. (ii), we get $\frac{(2 y)^{2}}{4}+y^{2}=1 \Rightarrow \frac{4 y^{2}}{4}+y^{2}=1$ $=$ $2 y^{2}=1 \Rightarrow y=\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ $\therefore$ From $\mathrm{E} q$ (i), $x=\pm \sqrt{2}$ $\therefore \quad P\left(\sqrt{2} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ and $Q\left(-\sqrt{2},-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ Equation of circle with $P Q$ as diameter is $$ \begin{array}{l} (x-\sqrt{2})(x+\sqrt{2})+\left(y-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\left(y+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \\ \Rightarrow \quad x^{2}-2+y^{2}-\frac{1}{2}=0 \Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}=\frac{5}{2} \end{array} $$
